faq.q: What is the origin of Aaban?

No — the underlying form is Persian, not Arabic.
Aaban can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Persian-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Aaban should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Ābān is a Persian month name, not a Quranic Arabic form.

faq.q: What does Aaban mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Aaban is rendered آبان and carries the sense آبان، ماه پارسی.
A romanized syllable approximation is aa-ban. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Aaban?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Aaban, aaban, aban. Script forms are آبان, آبَان, आबान.

faq.q: Is Aaban a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
